question: After the four blockers are fixed and live proof is added, should OpenClaw own an opt-in bundled surface that serves approved agent-authored widget assets through an unauthenticated static route and grants capabilities through a parent iframe bridge?
rationale: The implementation can be mechanically repaired, but accepting this permanent bundled security boundary and its operator-approval model requires explicit repository ownership rather than an automated correctness judgment.

options.title: Fix and accept the boundary
options.body: Require all findings, adversarial regression coverage, and redacted live browser diagnostics before approving the bundled custom-widget design.

options.title: Land built-in Workspaces only
options.body: Remove custom widget scaffolding, approval, unauthenticated serving, and prompt bridging while retaining the SQLite workspace, CLI, tools, grid, and built-in widgets.

options.title: Pause the bundled feature
options.body: Keep the tracking issue open but do not land this PR until maintainers choose a different extension or trust model for agent-authored UI.

recommendation.title: Fix and accept the boundary
recommendation.body: Require all findings, adversarial regression coverage, and redacted live browser diagnostics before approving the bundled custom-widget design.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the consolidated integration, are assigned on the PR, and have the strongest recent history across the affected runtime and UI surfaces.
